full_judgment:
2. Rule has been issued in writ petition No. 3488 of 2000 in the following terms: "A Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondent Nos. 1-6 to show cause as to why the impugned acquisition proceedings contained in the notice under section 3 of Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Properties Ordinance, 1982 (Annexure-F) in Land Acquisition Case No. 1 of 1999-2000 in respect of acquisition of lands measuring 6.56 acres contained in RS Plot Nos. 23-27, 29 and 41 in RS Khatin Nos. 35, 13, 15, 37, 39 and 38 of Mouza Uttar Ramchandrapur within PS Saver, District-Dhaka in favour of one Udyog Multipurpose Co-operative Society's proposed Niribili Housing Scheme should not be declared to have been without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Courts may seem fit and proper." 

 "A Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned Gazette Notification under the signature of respondent No. 5 so far it relates to the acquisition of land of the petitioners measuring 2.00 acres situated in RS Plot No. 25 in RS Khatian Nos. 15 of Mouza Uttar Ramchandrapur under Saver Police Station (now police Station Ashulia), District-Dhaka in connection with LA Case No. 1 of 1999-2000 shall not be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and why the Respondents shall not be directed to release the acquired 2.00 acres of land situated in RS Plot No. 25 in RS Khatian No. 15 of Mouza Uttar Ramchandrapur under Savar Police Station, District-Dhaka in connection with LA Case No. 1 of 1999-2000 in favor of the petitioners effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Courts may seem fit and proper." 

 4. Short facts as disclosed in the writ petition No. 3488 of 2000 in short is that petitioner No. 1 after his retirement from government service purchased 2.00 acres of land in RS Plot No. 25 having RS Khatian No. 15 in Mouja Uttor Ramchandpur under Police Station vide registered sale deed No. 15071 dated 8-7-1997 with a view to construct residence for himself and for his five sons and daughters having no housing accommodation at Dhaka. After purchase he demarcated boundary, erected barbed were fencing, mutated his name in the record of right and paid government revenues. Similarly petitioner No. 2-5 also with a view to construct residence purchased 0.45 acres of land by separate deeds in their names in 1998. While they have been owning and possessing as mentioned above they came to know that LA case No. 1 of 1999-2000 has been commenced for acquiring an area of 6.55 acres of land covering the case plot for Udyog Multipurpose Co-operative Society Limited with a view to materialize a housing scheme. The said housing society earlier got acquired 1.50 acres of land for establishing housing scheme. On the proposal of the said housing society Deputy Commissioner Dhaka acquired 1.23 acres of land vide LA Case No. 06 of 1976-1977 purportedly with a view to provide civic facility but no step was taken towards that end. After commencement of acquisition proceeding No.1 of 1999-2000 Ministry of land through its senior Assistant Secretary at the instance of Ministry of land an inquiry was conducted by LA officials and others vide annexure E-1 which was sent by Additional Deputy Commissioner Dhaka to the ministry of land wherein recommendation has been made not to acquire the land as it is not necessary for development project because the project could be implemented in the earlier acquired land, inspite of that the acquisition proceeding has been commenced and notice under section 3 of the acquisition and requisition immovable property ordinance was served beyond the knowledge of the petitioners without issuing public notice but after prolonged search the petitioner collected a copy of the notice issued under section 3 of the ordinance. The proposed acquisition proceeding is not for any public purpose which is Cristal clear from the report submitted by the land acquisition officer and others. Subsequently a notice under section 6 of the acquisition and requisition of immovable property ordinance, 1982 was served beyond the petitioner's knowledge and on coming to know about the said notice the petitioner filed objection against the said process and, as such, the petitioners were constrained to filed the instant writ petition. 

 5. Respondent No. 5 by filing an affidavit-in-opposition stated that with a view to establish hospital, educational institution, community center, religious and other welfare institution at the auspicious of Niribili Housing Scheme an area of 2.09 acres of land was acquired from RS plot No. 25 along with other land of Mouza Uttar Ramchandrapur vide LA case No.1 of 1999-2000 and after acquisition of the land the said was duly handed over to Udyog Multipurpose Co-operative Society upon observing all formalities. After the commencement of the acquisition proceeding notice under section 3 of the ordinance was properly affixed and served and no objection having been filed, notice under section 6 of the ordinance has been issued on 22-2-2000. Thereafter against notification regarding the acquisition of land was published as no order of stay passed by the Hon'ble High Court Division has been served upon respondent No. 5. It is further stated that Udyog Multipurpose Co-operative "Society Limited has allotted most of their plots to the members of the society who took possession accordingly but due to lack of civic facilities namely market, Mosque, Hospital etc the allottees did not construct houses in their plots. It is further stated that a total quantum of 5.56 acres of land of Mouza of Uttar Ramchandrapur was proposed to be acquired for Udyog Co-operative Society and after due approval in 51st meeting of central land allocation committee ministry of land issued direction for completing land acquisition proceeding and, as such, after completion of the procedure the acquired land has been handed over to Udyog Multipurpose Co-operative Society and hence the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 7. In writ petition No. 6348 of 2011, the heirs of writ petitioner No. 1 of writ petition No. 3488 of 2000 being petitioner Nos. 1-4 and along with 2 others as petitioners asserted the same facts as advanced in earlier writ petition and challenged the gazette notification dated 10-8-2006 issued under signature No. 5 so far it relates to acquisition of 2.00 acres of land in plot No. 25 having Khatian No. 15 under Mouza Uttar Ramchandrapur, within Savar Police Station present Ashulia Police Station, District-Dhaka. 

 11. Mr SM Mahbubul Islam, learned advocate appearing for the petitioner in writ petition No. 6348 of 2011 submits that notice under section 3 issued in LA Case No. 01 of 1999-2000 is vague and indefinite as it is mentioned in the notice that the property in question is needed or lightly to be needed for Niribili Housing scheme keeping in both the options which is illegal, lacking application of mind and, as such, the said notice is of no legal effect. He next submits that the impugned acquisition and consequent gazette notification has been issued acquiring the land of petitioners for not any public purpose or public interest which has been done at the behest to some government officials to give benefit to their relation and friends and, as such, the said proceeding is malafide having not public purpose and, as such, is liable to be declared illegal and is of no legal effect. 

 12. The learned advocate next submits that the acquisition in question is violative of the fundamental right of the petitioner grant it under article 42(1) of the constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and, as such, the impugned acquisition and consequent gazette notification to be declared as illegal and is of no legal effect. Learned advocate for the petitioner argued that in the report submitted by land Acquisition Officers and others at the instances of Ministry of law it is clearly mentioned that the proposed acquisition is not public purpose and the land acquired is earlier acquisition case for the Udyog co-operative Society has not been utilized by them and, as such, it is incumbent upon the acquiring authority to take cognizance of the said report and drop acquisition proceeding but instead they completed gazette notification regarding the acquired property which is illegal, malafide, ultra virus and is of no legal effect. Learned advocate pointed that the acquisition proceeding has been carried on for the benefit of some individual which is opposed to public policy and which is not for public purpose and, as such, the acquisition in question is liable to be struck down. 

 14. Mr Yousuf Hossain Humayun, learned counsel appearing for respondent No. 8 submits that with a view to establish hospital, educational institution, community center, religious and other welfare institution at the auspicious of Niribili Housing Scheme an area of 2.09 acres of land was acquired from RS plot No. 25 along with other land of Mouza Uttar Ramchandrapur vide LA case No.01 of 1999-2000 and after acquisition, the said land was duly handed over to Udyog Multipurpose Co-operative Society upon observing all formalities. He next submits that after the commencement of the acquisition proceeding notice under section 3 of the ordinance was properly affixed and served and no objection having been filed, notice section 6 of the ordinance has been issued on 22-2-2000. He further submits that notice regarding issuance of order of stay passed by the Hon'ble High Court division was not served upon respondent No. 5 and, as such, gazette notification regarding acquisition has been published. He also further submits that Udyog Multipurpose Co-operative "Society Limited has allotted most of their plots to the members of the society who took possession accordingly but due to lack of civic facilities namely market, Mosque, Hospital etc the allottees did not construct houses in their plots. He argued that a total quantum of 5.56 acres of land of Mouza of Uttar Ramchandrapur was proposed to be acquired for Udyog co-operative Society and after due approval in 51st meeting of central land allocation committee, Mnistry of land issued direction for completing land acquisition proceeding and, as such, after completion of all procedures the acquired land has been handed over to Udyog Multipurpose co-operative Society and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 15. Having gone through the writ petitioners, affidavit-in-oppositions and annexures it appears that the acquisition proceeding has been initiated to acquire land for Niribili Housing scheme which is a project of Udyog Multipurpose society vide LA case No.1 of 1999-2000. In the feasibility study report submitted in writ Petition No. 6348 of 2011 annexure-D it is stated that earlier 1.23 acres of land had been acquired for Niribili Housing scheme being run by Udyog Multipurpose society Ltd. vide LA case No. 06/76-77 and possession was made over to the requiring body but till date no installation has been carried out in the said acquired land and infrastructural development namely road, water supply and gas connections as well as other civic facilities has not been provided. The requiring body has huge land in the vicinity where the proposed project can be materialized. So from the said report it is explicitly clear that the land earlier acquired for the purpose of materialization of project remained vacant as yet having no infrastructural facilities although the same has been acquired about 25 years ago from the instant acquisition proceeding from which it can be inferred that the purpose for acquisition of land is anything but public purpose. In the said report it is clearly mentioned that the Udyog Multi-purpose co-operative society has other chunk of land where such project can be materialized and so it is also clear that the purpose of the said society is not to materialize project for the betterment of the people at large, rather to amass property for material gain and, as such, the proposed project cannot be termed for public purpose. In the case of Malik Mehdi Kabir vs Rabitat-al-Alam-aj-Islami, 65 DLR AD 109 it is held that: 

 "The explanation public purpose, is therefore, construed according to the times in which particular legislation is enacted is no construed. The acquisition of the immovable property has to be held to have been made for a public purpose and not otherwise. In this particular case, it is seen that the acquisition has been made not for any public purpose rather it is meant for private purpose for office complex of a non-government organization and the acquisition is not needed for public purpose. The High Court Division has totally over looked this aspect of the matter." 

 18. It is stated in the writ petition that the petitioner No. 1 of writ petition No. 3488 of 2000 being retired government official purchased certain quantum of land out of the case land for construction of his residential abode and other petitioners also purchased lands with a view to use for their own necessity and, as such, the case land cannot be taken away from them in the garb of public purpose which has been proved to be for ulterior purpose of the cooperative society in question. The petitioners have got unfettered right to enjoy their property as per article 42 of the constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. 

 19. It is also advanced on behalf of the petitioners that notice issued under section 3 of the acquisition and requisition of immovable property ordinance, 1982 is flawed and in effective as definite purpose of acquisition has not been spelt out. It is mentioned that the property may be used or likely to be used in future which is proximate and, as such, not sustainable. In the case of Sanjkar Gopal Chatterjee vs The Additional Commissioner, Dhaka Division, 41 DLR 326 it is held that: "Acquisition for a co-operative society per se is not a public purpose. The purpose of which the co-operative society proposes to used the acquired and is the ultimate test for a decision as to whether the acquisition is for a public purpose or not. There is a total lack of disclosure in the Notice under section 3 as to for what purpose the cooperative society needs the acquired land. The need to state the precise public purpose is imperative, because under section 4 of the ordinance any person interested in the disputed property has the right to object to the acquisition of the property challenging the public purpose stated therein, but if no specific public purpose is stated in the notice then the right given to the objection under section 4 rendered nugatory and illusory." 

 20. It is specifically asserted that in the writ petition that the acquisition proceeding has been initiated at the behest of some interested government officials with a view to offer benefit to their next of kin which has not been specifically refuted by the respondents rather from the report submitted by land acquisition officers and others wherein they specifically asserted that the proposed land is not necessary for public purpose and in the report it is specifically mentioned that the co-operative society has huge land in the vicinity of the land of acquisition proceeding. So it is clear that acquisition proceeding has been initiated with malafide motive and by colorable exercise of power which, cannot be sustained. In the case of Abdur Rouf vs Abdul Hakim 17 DLR (SC) 515 it is held that: 

 24. The impugned acquisition proceeding contained in the notice under section 3 of Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Properties Ordinance, 1982 (Annexure-F) in Land Acquisition Case No. 1 of 1999-2000 in respect of acquisition of lands measuring 6.56 acres contained in RS Plot Nos. 23-27, 29 and 41 in RS khatian Nos. 35, 13, 15, 37, 39 and 38 of Mouza Uttar Ramchandrapur within PS Saver, District-Dhaka in favour of one Udyog Multipurpose Co-operative Society's proposed Niribili Housing Scheme is declared to have been initiated and carried without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 25. Equally the impugned gazette notification dated 10-8-2006 (Annexure-A) issued under signature No. 5 so far it relates to acquisition of land of the petitioners measuring 2.00 acres situated in RS Plot No. 25 in RS Khatian No. 15 of Mouza Uttar Ramchandrapur under Savar Police Station (now Police Station Ashulia), District-Dhaka in connection With LA Case No. 1 of 1999-2001 is declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and respondents are directed to release the said 2.00 acres of land acquired in connection with LA case No.1 of 1999-2000 in favour of the petitioners.
